# CEO Plan: User Dashboard Page
Generated by /plan-ceo-review (via /autoplan) on 2026-09-10
Branch: main | Mode: SELECTIVE EXPANSION
Repo: gstack-autoplan-chain-ZdZS9F (local, no remote)

## Vision

### 10x Check
The 10x version is not a bigger dashboard. It is a dashboard that already knows the member's next item: "Resume: <assigned item title>" is the first thing on the page, one click from login, with notifications and activity as supporting context below. That requires action ranking and a per-member "next item" query that do not exist today. It is the natural Phase 2 (deferred as TODO T-D), and this plan's per-section envelope + independent panel components leave room for it without a rewrite.

## Problem and metric
Members visit three pages after login to find their next item (median 75s in a team walkthrough). Success measure: login-to-first-completed-task, target 45s, guardrails completed-task rate and permission-error rate.

Decisions in this review:
- The production baseline is computed from the existing `login`, `action start`, `action completion` events before any cohort opens (no new instrumentation is needed for the baseline; the new events below are needed for exposure attribution).
- The metric is segmented by action ID. Primary target: time to "resume assigned work". Create and invite are reported separately.
- The flag-off cohort is the control. The metric is compared per cohort (flag on vs flag off, same period), not only against the historical baseline.

## Alternatives considered
- A. Quick Actions strip + unread badge in the existing shell, no new page (Completeness 4/10): fastest hypothesis test, but does not deliver the stated feature and touches the shared shell.
- B. Dashboard page + one aggregate endpoint with per-section result envelopes (9/10): chosen. Keeps the stated backend shape; partial failure is explicit.
- C. Dashboard page + three per-panel endpoints (9/10): simplest failure semantics, three round trips. Close call with B; surfaced as Taste T2 at the /autoplan final gate. Flip trigger if B is kept: if the staging p95 gate fails because the aggregate's latency is dominated by one slow section that cannot be fixed at the source, switch to C.

## Contracts fixed by this review

### GET /api/dashboard
- Auth: existing session cookie + workspace membership middleware. Member and workspace IDs come from the request context only; a `workspaceId` query parameter is ignored. Unauthenticated → 401 (client redirects to login). Not a member → 403 (page-level "no access"). Feature flag off → 404 (client falls back to the current landing page).
- 200 body: `{ fetchedAt, activity, notifications, quickActions }`.
  - `Section<T> = { status: "ok", data: T } | { status: "error", code: "timeout" | "unavailable" | "internal", retryable: boolean }`.
  - `notifications.data = { items: NotificationItem[], unreadCount: number }`.
  - `quickActions.data = QuickAction[]` containing only actions whose server-side eligibility predicate passed; a throwing predicate omits that action and logs a warning with `actionId`.
  - A null or undefined repository result is converted to `{ status: "error", code: "internal", retryable: true }` and logged at error level; it is never returned as `ok`.
- Composition: the three repository calls run concurrently (`Promise.allSettled`), each with a 2s hard timeout that yields `code: "timeout", retryable: true`. The 2s timeout is the worst-case ceiling; the rollout gate (p95 < 500ms) measures typical latency. If the gate fails, fix or split the slow section; do not loosen the gate.
- Item counts: each section requests the existing first page (20 items + cursor); the client renders at most 10 and shows a "View all" link to the existing full page. The dashboard never paginates.

- `activity.data = { items: ActivityItem[] }` where `ActivityItem` is the existing activity list row type returned by the existing repository first page (reuse the type; do not define a new one).

### Mark all as read
- Uses the existing member-scoped, CSRF-protected, idempotent bulk-read API, which already accepts a snapshot time and marks only notifications at or before it (stated in the existing contracts). Request carries `snapshotAt = response.fetchedAt`.
- Two behaviors must be verified against the existing handler in the Eng phase and are **additions to that endpoint if absent** (backward-compatible, no migration): (a) the server clamps `snapshotAt` to ≤ now; (b) the response includes the new `unreadCount`. If (b) is absent and not added, the client derives `unreadCount` from the follow-up refetch only.
- Client flow: confirm in `MarkAllReadDialog` (existing Dialog primitive) → snapshot the current `notifications.data` value → optimistic flip (all rows read, `unreadCount = 0`) → POST → on success apply the response `unreadCount` if present, show a success toast, then refetch once; on csrf/network/5xx failure restore the snapshot and show an error toast whose Retry reopens the dialog (the flow retakes the snapshot). Confirm button is disabled while submitting. The button stays rendered but disabled at 0 unread so focus return has a target. The button is not rendered while the notifications section is not `status: "ok"`.
- Toast queue: max 3, drop-oldest.

### Client fetch behavior (`useDashboard`)
- In-flight requests are aborted on unmount (AbortController).
- Refetch triggers: the "Last updated · Refresh" control; `document.visibilityState` becoming `visible`, debounced to at most once per 30s; Retry on a page-level error or on any panel-level error (panel Retry refetches the whole aggregate; there is one endpoint); once after a bulk-read completes (success or failure).
- Mutation window: while a bulk-read POST is in flight, all refetch triggers are suppressed (Refresh and panel Retry controls disabled; visibility refetch deferred until the mutation settles). No GET is issued during the mutation window.
- Sequence guard: every request carries a monotonically increasing sequence number; a mutation bumps it when it starts and again when it settles; any response whose sequence is lower than the latest applied sequence is discarded. Together with the mutation window this guarantees no GET issued before or during the mutation can overwrite the post-mutation state.
- `dashboard_viewed` fires once per page mount, never on refetch.
- Empty-state CTAs: the notifications empty state links to the top eligible quick action if `quickActions.status === "ok"` and non-empty; otherwise, and always for the activity empty state, it links to item creation via the existing route.

### All-sections-failed behavior
The page renders a page-level error ("Dashboard unavailable") with a Retry control and direct links to the existing Activity, Notifications, and Create pages. The post-login redirect is unchanged (the member is still on /dashboard); the flag is the rollback lever if this state persists.

### Analytics events (IDs and counts only, never titles or bodies)
- `dashboard_viewed` — once per page mount.
- `dashboard_panel_state{panel ∈ {activity, notifications, quickActions}, state ∈ {ok, empty, error}, trigger ∈ {initial, refresh, visible, retry, post_mutation}}` — once per panel per completed fetch (initial and every refetch).
- `quick_action_clicked{actionId}` — on click.
- `notifications_mark_all_read{result ∈ {success, error_csrf, error_network, error_5xx, error_other}}` — once per submit.
- Existing `login`, `action start`, `action completion`, `permission error` events are reused for the metric.

### Observability
- Logs: handler entry/exit with requestId, memberId, workspaceId, per-section status and duration; section errors at error level with class and stack.
- Metrics: `dashboard_request_duration_seconds{section}`, `dashboard_section_error_total{section,code}`, `dashboard_all_sections_failed_total`, `notifications_mark_all_read_total{result}`.
- Alerts: section error rate > 2% over 5m (page); p95 > 1s over 10m (warn); all-sections-failed > 0 in 5m (page).
- Runbook: `docs/runbooks/dashboard.md`.

### Rollout
Flag `dashboard_landing` gates both the `/dashboard` route and the post-login redirect. Order: deploy flag off → production baseline captured from existing events (window ends before any cohort, including internal, is enabled) → internal cohort → staging p95 < 500ms and DB pool headroom under a login-burst test → 5% → 25% → 100%, with completed-task rate and permission-error rate (by actionId) as guardrails. Rollback: flag off (seconds); code revert only if the flag path is broken. No migrations.

## Scope Decisions

| # | Proposal | Effort | Decision | Reasoning |
|---|----------|--------|----------|-----------|
| E1 | Relative timestamps with absolute time in `<time datetime>`/title | S | ACCEPTED | In blast radius, < 1 day; makes recency scannable (hierarchy) |
| E2 | Optimistic mark-all-read with rollback + error toast | S | ACCEPTED | In blast radius, < 1 day; removes a wait on the one mutation |
| E3 | Refetch when tab becomes visible (debounced 30s) + "Last updated · Refresh" | S | ACCEPTED | In blast radius; a "home" page left open goes stale and misleads on unread state. No stale-data complaint evidence exists yet because the page does not exist; keep, and watch `dashboard_panel_state` refetch counts |
| E4 | Empty states that name the next action | S | ACCEPTED | Empty states already in scope; copy + one link |
| E5 | Unread badge in global nav | S | DEFERRED | Outside blast radius (shared shell) |
| E6 | Per-item mark read | M | DEFERRED | Needs a per-item mutation API that does not exist |
| E7 | Undo for mark-all-read | M | DEFERRED | Needs an unread mutation API |
| E8 | Keyboard shortcuts | S | SKIPPED | Not on the metric; adds a11y surface |
| E9 | Prefetch quick-action routes on hover | S | SKIPPED | Marginal; revisit if route transition > 300ms |
| E10 | "Resume: next item" hero (10x) | L | DEFERRED | New ranking service; Phase 2 |

## Accepted Scope (added to this plan)
- Relative timestamps on activity and notification rows.
- Optimistic mark-all-read with snapshot/rollback and toast feedback.
- Refetch on visible (debounced) plus a visible "Last updated · Refresh" control.
- Empty states pointing at the top eligible quick action / item creation.

## Shared primitives introduced
- `PanelFrame`: loading/empty/error/ok wrapper used by all three panels.
- `ToastProvider` + `Toast`: app-root `aria-live="polite"` region outside any dialog focus trap, queue max 3, reduced-motion safe. The accessibility policy requires a live region for non-blocking feedback, so some live-region component must exist; building it once at app root (rather than dashboard-local) is Taste T4 and may be overridden at the gate. T-E tracks app-wide adoption so it does not stay a single-use primitive.

## Deferred to TODOS.md
- T-A Global nav unread badge (E5) — depends on `notifications.data.unreadCount` from this endpoint.
- T-B Per-item mark-read (E6) — needs a member-scoped per-item mutation API.
- T-C Undo mark-all-read (E7) — needs an unread mutation API.
- T-D "Resume: next item" hero (E10) — Phase 2; needs ranking/eligibility service.
- T-E Adopt the toast primitive app-wide so it does not remain dashboard-only.
- T-F Per-member landing preference (dashboard vs last visited) — personalization plan.

## Taste decisions surfaced at the /autoplan Final Gate
Provisional means: the plan proceeds with the stated option through the remaining review phases; the user confirms or flips it once, at the gate.
- T1 Ship as one release vs phase strip-first (kept as stated).
- T2 Aggregate endpoint with envelope vs per-panel endpoints (kept; flip trigger above).
- T3 Keep the confirmation modal for mark-all-read vs single click (kept; no bulk-unread API makes the action one-way).
- T4 Shared toast primitive vs inline status text / dashboard-local toast (kept).
